paper.title: Online Learning of Optimally Diverse Rankings

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning of diverse rankings (cascading-click model with hidden query topics)
unmapped: Cascade feedback: the learner observes only the position of the first clicked item (partial semi-bandit), not all item relevances
Actions are ordered lists of L items out of N; reward is probability of at least one click
Hidden context: query topic m(n) drawn i.i.d. from unknown distribution phi over M topics, revealed only a posteriori upon a click
Items partitioned into M known topics; theta_km = 0 if item k not in topic m
Lower bound is proved in an easier model where an oracle reveals phi and the topic of each query after the round
settings.definition_quote: The set $\mathcal{ N}$ of $N$ items is partitioned into $M$ non-overlapping subsets ... The decision maker is aware of this partition. ... we assume that $\theta_{km}=0$ whenever $k\notin \mathcal{ N}_m$ ... the topic of the $n$-th query, denoted by $m(n)$, is unknown. $(m(n))_{n\ge 1}$ is an i.i.d sequence ... with distribution $\phi$ ... The user then scans the items in the list in order, and clicks on the first relevant item, if any. ... $R^\pi(T) = T\mu(u^\star) - \EE[\sum_{n=1}^T \mu(u^{\pi}(n))]$.

symbols.I_1k: Bernoulli KL I(nu(L|y^k)+delta, nu(L|u*)), y^k = u* with last item replaced by k
symbols.I_2k: Bernoulli KL I(phi_{h(k)} theta_{k h(k)} + delta, phi_{h(k)} theta_{L_k h(k)} - delta)
symbols.C_NLdelta: constant C(N,L,delta) bounded explicitly in the theorem in terms of N, L, delta and constants C_1, C_2
symbols.delta: analysis parameter delta in (0, Delta) (not a failure probability)

conditions: k > L is a suboptimal item (k not in u*)
delta in (0, Delta) where Delta is an instance-dependent separation

source.label: th:DiversiPIERegret
source.quote: There exists a constant $C(N,L,\delta)$ depending on $N, L$ and $\delta$, and a round $n_0$ such that under the LDR algorithm, we have: $\forall T>n_0$, $\delta>0$ and $\forall k>L$, $\EE[\sum_{n=1}^T\mathbbm{1}[k\in u(n)]\leq \frac{f(T) }{ I(\nu(L|y^k) + \delta, \nu(L|u^\star))}+ \frac{f(T)}{I(\phi_{h(k)} \theta_{k h(k)}+\delta, \phi_{h(k)} \theta_{L_k h(k)}-\delta)}+ C(N,L,\delta)$.

results.notes: Bound on the expected number of rounds a suboptimal item k is displayed. Constant C(N,L,delta) has an explicit (long) upper bound involving unspecified finite constants C_1, C_2. Section referred to as Theorem 3.1 in the appendix.

symbols.Delta_y_k: mu(u*) - mu(y^k), y^k = u* with last item replaced by item k
symbols.Delta_w_k: mu(u*) - mu(w^k), w^k = k prepended to u*
symbols.I_2k: Bernoulli KL I(phi_{h(k)} theta_{k h(k)} + delta, phi_{h(k)} theta_{L_k h(k)} - delta)

conditions: sum over suboptimal items k > L (N - L items)
results.notes: Sum is over suboptimal items, giving the O((N-L) log T) scaling claimed. sum_subopt here ranges over items not in u*. Proof's final display uses I(nu(L|y^k)+delta, nu(L|u*)) without -delta; recorded as in theorem statement.

symbols.Delta_u_k: mu(u*) - mu(u^k), u^k = best list containing item k in the first slot
symbols.I_min_k: min over lambda in B_k(theta) of Bernoulli KL I(theta_{k h(k)}, lambda_{k h(k)})

conditions: sum over suboptimal items k > L
uniformly good: R(T) = o(T^a) for all a > 0 on all instances
holds even if an oracle reveals phi and the topic of each query after each round

source.label: th:LowBoundRew1
source.quote: For any parameter $(\phi,\theta)\in\Lambda\times \Theta$, and for any uniformly good policy $\pi\in \Pi$, we have: $\lim\inf_{T\to\infty} \frac{R^\pi(T)}{\log(T)} \ge \sum_{k > L} \frac{\mu(u^\star) - \mu(u^k)}{\min_{\lambda\in B_k(\theta)} I(\theta_{kh(k)},\lambda_{kh(k)})}.$

results.notes: Derived via Graves-Lai in an oracle-aided model; scales as Theta((N-L) log T).
